meta.purpose: Human- and LLM-readable decoding of the abbreviated cortical region labels used in connectivity_data.json. Given a natural-language user query (e.g. 'the area for face recognition' or 'where is movement controlled'), an LLM can match against the 'description'/'keywords' fields here and narrow down to the actual abbreviation label, then prepend 'L_' (left) or 'R_' (right) to address a specific hemisphere.
meta.atlas: Marmoset Brain Mapping (MBM) / Brain-MINDS cortical parcellation, 106 areas per hemisphere. Nomenclature is a variant of Paxinos G, Watson C, Petrides M, Rosa M, Tokuno H. 'The Marmoset Brain in Stereotaxic Coordinates' (Elsevier Academic Press, 2012).
meta.label_convention: Region labels in connectivity_data.json are prefixed 'L_' (left hemisphere) or 'R_' (right hemisphere). Strip the prefix to look up the base abbreviation below. The 'A' prefix on many names means 'Area' (Brodmann-style cytoarchitectonic area number).
meta.species_note: Coordinates and areas describe the common marmoset (Callithrix jacchus) cortex; functional roles are inferred from marmoset/primate neuroanatomy and are homologous but not identical to human areas.
meta.confidence_notes: 'Pri' is the ctbl spelling of Paxinos 'Pir' = piriform (primary olfactory) cortex — confirmed from the atlas source. One label remains a best-interpretation and should be confirmed against the atlas if used for critical work: 'SB' (interpreted as subiculum, a hippocampal-formation output region), which does not appear in the Paxinos area list.
sources: Paxinos et al. 2012, The Marmoset Brain in Stereotaxic Coordinates
Reser et al. 2013, Cereb Cortex 23:1901-22 (functional grouping scheme)

groups.DLP: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex — executive control, working memory, planning, attention, eye movements.
groups.VLP: Ventrolateral prefrontal cortex — response inhibition, value-based decisions, vocal/communication control.
groups.OFC: Orbitofrontal cortex — reward valuation, taste and smell, emotion, flexible goal-directed behaviour.
groups.MPC: Medial prefrontal / anterior cingulate cortex — emotion, motivation, autonomic regulation, conflict monitoring.
groups.MPM: Motor and premotor cortex — planning and execution of voluntary movement.
groups.INS: Insula and rostral lateral sulcus — interoception, visceral/autonomic sensation, taste, emotion.
groups.SSC: Somatosensory cortex — touch, body sensation, proprioception.
groups.AUD: Auditory cortex — hearing and sound processing.
groups.LIT: Lateral and inferior temporal cortex — high-level vision (objects, faces), auditory association, multisensory/social perception.
groups.VTC: Ventral temporal / medial temporal cortex — memory, recognition, smell, spatial context.
groups.PCR: Posterior cingulate, medial and retrosplenial cortex — spatial memory, navigation, default-mode/self-referential processing.
groups.PPC: Posterior parietal cortex — spatial attention, reaching/grasping, sensorimotor integration, eye-hand coordination.
groups.VIS: Visual cortex — processing of visual information from primary vision through motion, colour and form.

A10.description: The very front tip of the brain (frontal pole). Supports the most abstract executive functions: multitasking, planning for the future, evaluating options, and holding goals in mind.

A9.description: Dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Central to working memory (holding information 'in mind') and top-down cognitive control of behaviour.

A46.full_name: Area 46 (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, principal sulcus region)
A46.description: Prefrontal area around the principal sulcus, classically linked to spatial working memory and sustained attention.

8a.full_name: Area 8a (dorsal prefrontal / frontal eye field region)
8a.description: Part of the frontal eye field complex. Controls voluntary eye movements (saccades), gaze shifting and visual spatial attention.

8b.description: Dorsomedial prefrontal region adjacent to the frontal eye fields; involved in attention orienting and oculomotor control.

A47L.full_name: Area 47 lateral (old area 12), ventrolateral prefrontal cortex
A47L.description: Ventrolateral prefrontal cortex. Involved in response inhibition, evaluating rewards/outcomes and flexible rule-based behaviour.

A47M.full_name: Area 47 medial (old area 12), ventral prefrontal / orbital
A47M.description: Medial part of ventrolateral prefrontal cortex, bordering the orbital surface; contributes to value-based choice and emotional evaluation.

A45.description: Inferior frontal cortex, part of the primate homologue of Broca's region. Linked to vocalization/communication and cognitive control of behaviour.

ProM.description: Transitional motor cortex on the frontal operculum near the insula. Associated with orofacial movement and vocalization control.

A32V.full_name: Area 32 ventral (medial prefrontal / pregenual anterior cingulate)
A32V.description: Ventral part of medial prefrontal area 32. Involved in emotion regulation, decision-making and self-referential processing.

A32D.description: Dorsal part of area 32 on the medial wall; contributes to cognitive control, conflict monitoring and emotion.

A14.description: Ventromedial prefrontal cortex on the medial orbital surface. Regulates autonomic responses, emotion and the value of outcomes.

A24a.description: Anterior cingulate cortex. Part of the emotional/motivational limbic system; autonomic and affective regulation.

A24b.description: Anterior cingulate cortex, involved in emotion, effort/motivation and behavioural drive.

A24cd.full_name: Areas 24c/24d (dorsal anterior cingulate / cingulate motor region)
A24cd.description: Dorsal/caudal anterior cingulate including the cingulate motor area. Links motivation to movement — effort-based action and motor control.

A25.description: Subgenual cingulate cortex beneath the corpus callosum. Key node for autonomic/visceral regulation and mood; implicated in depression in humans.

A11L.description: Lateral orbitofrontal cortex. Represents the reward value of stimuli and supports goal-directed, flexible choice.

A11M.description: Medial orbitofrontal cortex; reward valuation and emotional evaluation of outcomes.

A13L.description: Posterior-lateral orbitofrontal cortex. Integrates taste, smell and reward signals to guide flexible behaviour.

A13M.description: Medial part of posterior orbitofrontal area 13; emotion, reward and outcome valuation.

Gu.description: Primary taste cortex. Processes taste quality and intensity (sweet, salty, sour, bitter).

Opro.description: Primitive transitional cortex on the caudal orbital surface near the insula. Integrates olfactory and limbic (emotional) information.

OPAl.description: The most primitive (allocortical) part of the orbital cortex, closely tied to the olfactory system and emotion.

A6D.description: Dorsal premotor cortex. Plans and prepares limb movements, especially reaching, using sensory cues.

A6M.description: Supplementary motor area on the medial wall. Organizes movement sequences and self-initiated (internally generated) movements.

A6V.description: Ventral premotor cortex. Controls grasping and hand/mouth actions and links sensory input to movement (sensorimotor transformation).

A4M.full_name: Area 4 medial (primary motor cortex, medial part)
A4M.description: Primary motor cortex, medial part. Directly drives voluntary movement of the trunk and hindlimb (leg) muscles.

A4L.full_name: Area 4 lateral (primary motor cortex, lateral part)
A4L.description: Primary motor cortex, lateral part. Directly drives voluntary movement of the face, mouth and forelimb (hand/arm) muscles.

S1M.description: Primary somatosensory cortex (touch). The medial part maps sensation from the trunk and lower body/legs.

S1D.description: Primary somatosensory cortex (touch), dorsal part; maps sensation from the arm/hand region of the body.

S1V.description: Primary somatosensory cortex (touch), ventral part; maps sensation from the face and mouth.

S2a.description: Higher-order (secondary) somatosensory cortex. Processes texture, shape and integrates touch for object recognition by feel.

S2b.description: Secondary somatosensory cortex; tactile feature processing and multisensory touch integration.

Core.description: Primary auditory cortex. First cortical stage of hearing; encodes basic sound features and is tonotopically organized (mapped by frequency/pitch).

BeltM.description: Secondary auditory cortex surrounding the core (medial belt). Processes more complex sound patterns than the primary area.

BeltL.description: Secondary auditory cortex surrounding the core (lateral belt). Analyzes sound features such as frequency sweeps and vocalization elements.

PBR.description: Higher-order auditory association cortex (rostral parabelt). Involved in identifying sounds and processing communication calls ('what' pathway).

PBC.description: Higher-order auditory association cortex (caudal parabelt). Contributes to sound localization and auditory spatial processing ('where' pathway).

STR.description: Rostral superior temporal cortex. Auditory and multisensory association region contributing to processing of voices and complex sounds.

AI.description: Anterior (agranular) insula. Processes visceral/autonomic body states, emotion and interoception ('gut feelings').

DI.description: Mid-insula (dysgranular). Integrates interoceptive, taste and multisensory body signals.

GI.description: Posterior (granular) insula. Primary interoceptive cortex representing internal bodily sensations such as temperature, pain and visceral state.

ReI.description: Posterior retroinsular cortex. Multisensory area processing vestibular (balance), somatosensory and auditory information.

PaIR.description: Transitional cortex between insula and temporal lobe (rostral). Links auditory/somatosensory input with visceral-emotional processing.

PaIC.description: Transitional insula-temporal cortex (caudal); multisensory and interoceptive integration.

Tpt.description: Cortex at the temporo-parietal junction near auditory areas. Involved in spatial hearing, auditory-spatial attention and multisensory integration.

TPOR.full_name: Temporo-parieto-occipital association area, rostral (superior temporal polysensory, STP)
TPOR.description: Superior temporal polysensory cortex (rostral). Integrates vision, hearing and touch; important for perceiving biological motion, actions and social cues.

TPOC.full_name: Temporo-parieto-occipital association area, caudal (superior temporal polysensory, STP)
TPOC.description: Superior temporal polysensory cortex (caudal). Multisensory integration and processing of moving social/visual stimuli.

FSTR.full_name: Fundus of the superior temporal sulcus area, rostral
FSTR.description: Part of the middle-temporal motion complex, in the depth of the superior temporal sulcus. Processes visual motion.

FSTC.full_name: Fundus of the superior temporal sulcus area, caudal
FSTC.description: Caudal fundal superior temporal area; visual motion analysis within the MT/MST motion complex.

TEa.full_name: Temporal area TE, subdivision a (inferotemporal cortex)
TEa.description: Inferotemporal visual cortex. High-level ('what') visual recognition of objects, shapes and faces.

TEb.full_name: Temporal area TE, subdivision b (inferotemporal cortex)
TEb.description: Inferotemporal visual cortex; recognition of complex objects and faces.

TEc.full_name: Temporal area TE, subdivision c (inferotemporal cortex)
TEc.description: Inferotemporal visual cortex; high-level object and face processing.

TEd.full_name: Temporal area TE, subdivision d (inferotemporal cortex)
TEd.description: Inferotemporal visual cortex; visual object and face recognition.

TEe.full_name: Temporal area TE, subdivision e (inferotemporal cortex)
TEe.description: Inferotemporal visual cortex; high-level visual recognition.

TEf.full_name: Temporal area TE, subdivision f (inferotemporal cortex)
TEf.description: Inferotemporal visual cortex; high-level visual recognition of objects and faces.

TPPro.description: Temporal pole. A hub for semantic memory (meaning of objects/words) and for social and emotional processing.

PrhR.description: Perirhinal cortex. Critical for recognition memory — judging whether an object has been seen before — and object familiarity.

PrhC.description: Perirhinal cortex (caudal); object recognition memory and visual associative memory.

Enta.description: Entorhinal cortex — the main gateway between the neocortex and the hippocampus. Essential for memory formation and spatial navigation (grid cells).

Entb.description: Entorhinal cortex; hippocampal input/output hub for memory and spatial coding.

PHGa.full_name: Parahippocampal gyrus, subdivision a (temporal areas TF/TH/TL)
PHGa.description: Parahippocampal cortex. Processes spatial context and scenes ('place' information) and supports contextual memory.

PHGb.full_name: Parahippocampal gyrus, subdivision b (temporal areas TF/TH/TL)
PHGb.description: Parahippocampal cortex; scene/context processing and contextual memory.

PHGc.full_name: Parahippocampal gyrus, subdivision c (temporal areas TF/TH/TL)
PHGc.description: Parahippocampal cortex; spatial/contextual memory and scene recognition.

Pri.description: Primary olfactory (piriform) cortex, which receives direct input from the olfactory bulb and represents smells/odour identity. (Paxinos abbreviation 'Pir'.)

SB.full_name: Subiculum (hippocampal formation output) — best interpretation, verify against atlas
SB.description: Interpreted as the subiculum, the main output region of the hippocampal formation. Involved in memory and spatial processing. Label is a best guess — confirm against the atlas source.

PEa.description: Superior parietal cortex. Uses body/limb position (proprioception) to guide reaching and coordinate movement.

PEb.description: Superior parietal cortex; body-position sense and sensorimotor control of reaching movements.

PF/PFGa.full_name: Parietal areas PF / PFG, subdivision a
PF/PFGa.description: Inferior parietal cortex. Integrates sensory and motor information for skilled hand actions; part of the action-observation ('mirror') system.

PF/PFGb.full_name: Parietal areas PF / PFG, subdivision b
PF/PFGb.description: Inferior parietal cortex; sensorimotor integration for actions and multisensory body representation.

PGa.description: Inferior parietal cortex. Involved in visuospatial attention, spatial awareness and eye-hand coordination.

PGb.description: Inferior parietal cortex; visuospatial attention and spatial cognition.

Opta.description: Transitional cortex between parietal and visual areas. Processes visual motion and spatial information for guiding movement.

Optb.description: Occipito-parietal transitional cortex; visual-spatial processing for action.

IPa.description: Intraparietal cortex. Planning of eye movements, reaching and grasping, and control of spatial attention.

IPb.description: Intraparietal cortex; sensorimotor transformations for reaching, grasping and gaze.

IPc.description: Intraparietal cortex; coordinates hand/eye movements and spatial attention.

IPd.description: Intraparietal cortex; visuomotor control and spatial attention.

A23a.description: Posterior cingulate cortex. A core node of the default-mode network; involved in memory retrieval, self-referential thought and spatial orientation.

A23b.description: Posterior cingulate cortex; default-mode processing, memory and internal attention.

A23V.description: Ventral posterior cingulate cortex; part of the default-mode network, linked to memory and self-related processing.

A29M.description: Retrosplenial cortex. Critical for spatial navigation, translating between self-centred and world-centred spatial maps, and episodic memory.

A30.description: Retrosplenial cortex. Supports spatial navigation, scene processing and memory-guided orientation.

A29V.description: Retrosplenial cortex (ventral); spatial navigation and memory.

A31.description: Posterior cingulate cortex (dorsal). Part of the default-mode network; involved in memory, self-processing and integration of information.

PGMa.full_name: Parietal area PG medial, subdivision a
PGMa.description: Medial posterior parietal cortex. Involved in spatial cognition, visually guided reaching and integration with the default-mode network.

PGMb.full_name: Parietal area PG medial, subdivision b
PGMb.description: Medial posterior parietal cortex; spatial processing and visuomotor integration.

ProSt.description: Prostriata — a primitive visual area near the retrosplenial cortex. Specialized for very fast processing of motion in the far peripheral visual field.

V1a.full_name: Primary visual cortex, subdivision a (V1, striate cortex)
V1a.description: Primary visual cortex (V1). The first cortical stage of vision; detects edges, orientation, contrast and basic visual features, retinotopically mapped.

V1b.full_name: Primary visual cortex, subdivision b (V1, striate cortex)
V1b.description: Primary visual cortex (V1). Basic visual feature detection (edges, orientation, contrast); represents another part of the visual field.

V2M.description: Second visual area (V2). Processes contours, textures, figure-ground segregation and combines features from V1.

V2L.description: Second visual area (V2), lateral part; contour, texture and form processing.

V2V.description: Second visual area (V2), ventral part; represents the upper visual field and processes form and texture.

V3D.description: Third visual area (V3), dorsal part. Contributes to processing of form and global motion / dynamic form.

V3L.description: Third visual area (V3), lateral part; form and motion processing.

V3V.description: Ventral V3 (area VP). Processes form and colour information for the upper visual field.

V4L.description: Fourth visual area (V4). A key stage for colour perception and for processing of complex shapes and form.

V4V.description: Ventral V4; colour and shape/form processing, part of the ventral 'what' visual pathway.

V5R.full_name: Visual area 5, rostral part (MT, middle temporal area)
V5R.description: Middle temporal area (MT/V5). Specialized for visual motion — direction and speed of moving objects.

V5C.full_name: Visual area 5, caudal part (MT, middle temporal area)
V5C.description: Middle temporal area (MT/V5), caudal part; detection of visual motion direction and speed.

V6R.description: Area V6 in medial occipital cortex. Processes wide-field visual motion and self-motion (optic flow) and feeds parietal reaching areas.

V6M.description: Area V6 (medial); wide-field motion and optic-flow processing for spatial vision.

V6D.description: Area V6 (dorsal); motion and optic-flow processing linked to visually guided movement.

A19DI.description: Higher-order (extrastriate) visual cortex of area 19. Intermediate visual processing of form and motion beyond V1/V2.

A19M.description: Medial extrastriate visual cortex (area 19). Higher-order visual processing, contributing to the dorsal visuospatial stream.

MST.description: Medial superior temporal area. Processes complex visual motion and optic flow (patterns of motion during self-movement); important for navigation and smooth eye tracking.
